reference.title: Markdown typical page structure
reference.shortdesc: A typical Markdown page follows standard Markdown structure:

section.p: A typical Markdown page follows standard Markdown structure:+++ title = "Alarm Notifier" description = "Configure and manage alarm notifications." author = "Documentation Team" keywords = ["alarms", "notifications", "monitoring"] +++ # Alarm Notifier Alarm Notifier controls how alarm notifications are delivered to users and external systems. ## Creating a New Alarm Notification To create a new alarm notification: 1. Click **Alarms**. 2. Click **Add Notification**. 3. Configure the notification settings. 4. Click **Save**. ![Alarm Configuration Screen](images/alarm-config.png)
The converter focuses on two key areas:

ol.li: Metadata (optional): The converter maps metadata fields to DITA metadata structures such as <title>, <shortdesc>, <author>, <keywords>, and topic <prolog> elements.
Markdown Content Body: The converter maps headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, hyperlinks, admonitions, and code blocks to the appropriate DITA topic body elements.

section.p: The markdown to DITA converter ignores the following elements:

ul.li: Content generated at build time rather than stored in Markdown source

section.note: The converter only processes content contained within the Markdown source files. Metadata, navigation structures, or content generated by site templates, themes, plugins, or build scripts are not converted unless explicitly supported by a custom conversion configuration.
